sentences.text: Udanoceratops was a large leptoceratopsid dinosaur, the largest known member of its family, reaching approximately 4 meters in length and weighing around 700 kilograms.

Its skull was deeper and more robust than relatives, featuring larger nasal cavities, a heavier beak, and smooth snout bones without horns or tubercles. Projections on the cheek bones likely supported a large patch of keratin.
The genus authority Kurzanov suggested that the teeth functioned only as cutting mechanisms.
The holotype specimen, discovered in the 1980s during the Joint Soviet-Mongolian Paleontological Expedition, was formally described by Sergei Kurzanov in 1992.

While some suggest Udanoceratops was semi-aquatic, its claw shape is more likely an adaptation for walking on soft substrates like sand dunes. Bipedal running is unlikely; if it ran, it likely did so on all fours and was slower than smaller relatives.
Kurzanov suggested that Udanoceratops engaged in ritual head-swinging confrontations between two individuals, likely males.

It belongs to the family Leptoceratopsidae, being the only Asian representative at the time alongside the North American Leptoceratops, Montanoceratops, and Prenoceratops. The genus and species authorities are both Kurzanov, 1992.

Fossils are known from the Djadochta Formation in Mongolia, an area also famous for Protoceratops and Velociraptor. The Udan-Sayr locality is part of this formation, dated to the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous, from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.

It is debated whether a large skull from the Bayan Mandahu Formation belongs to Udanoceratops; some researchers suspect it was misidentified as Protoceratops hellenikorhinus. The status of a juvenile specimen (PIN 4046/11) is debated, with some studies considering it an indeterminate leptoceratopsid rather than Udanoceratops. Gregory S. Paul suggested in 2016 that a break on the holotype skull was caused by the beak of another individual rather than ritual combat. V. S. Tereschenko argued that bipedal locomotion in Udanoceratops was very unlikely and that the assumption of short forelimbs lacked sufficient foundation.
